record.original_question: How can all Riemannian foliations of finite-dimensional differentiable manifolds be constructed?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional smooth (differentiable) manifold. A foliation $\mathcal{F}$ of $M$ of codimension $q$ is a partition of $M$ into immersed connected submanifolds (the leaves) such that there exists an atlas of charts $\varphi_i : U_i \to \mathbb{R}^{n-q} \times \mathbb{R}^q$ whose transition maps have the form $(x,y) \mapsto (f_{ij}(x,y), g_{ij}(y))$. The foliation $\mathcal{F}$ is called Riemannian if there exists a Riemannian metric $g_T$ on the normal bundle $\nu\mathcal{F} = TM/T\mathcal{F}$ (a transverse metric) which is holonomy invariant, i.e., for every vector field $X$ tangent to $\mathcal{F}$ the Lie derivative $\mathcal{L}_X g_T = 0$. Equivalently, locally there exist Riemannian submersions onto $q$-dimensional manifolds whose fibers are the plaques of $\mathcal{F}$, and the local transverse metrics agree under the transition maps.

Provide an explicit construction that produces, up to foliated isomorphism, all Riemannian foliations on all finite-dimensional smooth manifolds. That is, exhibit a procedure (with prescribed building blocks and gluing data) such that:
(i) every output of the procedure is a Riemannian foliation of some finite-dimensional smooth manifold, and
(ii) every Riemannian foliation of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold is, up to isomorphism of foliated manifolds, obtained as an output of the procedure.
artifact.status_search_result: A structural theory of Riemannian foliations has been developed (Molino's structure theorem describes a Riemannian foliation via a transverse parallelism on a bundle over $M$ and the closures of leaves), and various classification results exist in specific settings (e.g., on spheres, in low codimension, or for transversely homogeneous types). However, a single explicit construction yielding all Riemannian foliations of all finite-dimensional smooth manifolds is not established in the standard literature, and the question of a complete classification remains generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Molino, Riemannian Foliations
status_evidence.snippet: Molino's structure theorem describes Riemannian foliations via transverse parallelisms and leaf closures, providing a structural but not constructive classification.
status_evidence.claim: A structure theorem exists but does not give an explicit construction of all Riemannian foliations.
